open_questions[3]: NARROWED AT CYCLE 25, STILL OPEN. Fine-tuning and few-shot were both shown to sometimes worsen accuracy and calibration (gpt4o APT-extraction P/R 0.87->0.68 after fine-tuning; CVE-generation ECE 0.15->0.91, both re-verified exact this cycle) -- is this degradation specific to small fine-tuning dataset size / overfitting, or a general risk for CTI fine-tuning regardless of data volume? WHAT CYCLE 25 ESTABLISHED: the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting (checked explicitly), so it offers no answer, and the only sentence bearing on the fine-tuning set size came back ELIDED from the fetch ('We randomly select 70% of the dataset...70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning') and is therefore NOT verbatim-captured. Two concrete next steps: re-pull that split sentence verbatim, and note that the fine-tuning pool is bounded above by 350 reports either way, which makes small-data overfitting a live but unconfirmed explanation. === CYCLE 39: THE NAMED UNDONE STEP IS DISCHARGED, THE BOUND CYCLE 25 RECORDED WAS WRONG, AND THE UNDERLYING QUESTION NARROWS BUT STAYS OPEN. The split passage is now captured WHOLE AND UNELIDED, identical from two URL forms (arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and the unversioned render, which is v4), verbatim: 'Dataset division. We randomly select 70% of the dataset, thus mimicking the splitting which is typical of ML and DL model validations. In ML and DL, the splitting would have been in training, validation, and testing respectively in portions of 70%, 20%, and 10%. Since we do not train from scratch our model we assign 70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning and 30% for the testing. We employ this division to avoid overfitting both for fine-tuning and for few-shot learning, if the few-shot examples are gathered directly from the dataset on which testing is conducted.' CORRECTION TO CYCLE 25: the fine-tuning pool is NOT bounded above by 350 reports. It is bounded by 70% of 350 = 245 reports (AGENT-DERIVED; the paper prints only '# of reports: 350' and the percentages), and that 245 is SHARED with the few-shot example pool, so fine-tuning alone used at most 245 and possibly far fewer. Test set is 30% = 105 reports (AGENT-DERIVED). THE EXACT NUMBER OF REPORTS USED FOR FINE-TUNING IS ABSENT, confirmed against two URL forms. SO IS THE ENTIRE FINE-TUNING SETUP: no hyperparameters, no epoch count, no learning rate, no endpoint, no fine-tuning-set size appear anywhere in the paper, confirmed ABSENT by two fetches on two URL forms, each permitted to answer ABSENT. This is a real reporting limitation of src-0001 and had never been recorded. CYCLE 25's 'the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting' is CONFIRMED, but it must be scoped more precisely than cycle 25 scoped it: the word 'overfitting' DOES occur in the paper, twice, and both occurrences are about the SPLIT DESIGN rather than about the observed degradation -- the sentence above, and 'To control for prompt overfitting ... we evaluate the LLMs on the part of the dataset from which we do not gather any few-shot examples'. The paper invokes overfitting only as something its design controls FOR, never as an explanation of what it measured, and that control is asserted rather than measured. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS OPEN: whether the post-fine-tuning calibration collapse is a small-data or overfitting artefact CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM src-0001 AT ALL, because the paper reports neither the fine-tuning set size nor any fine-tuning configuration. A 245-report ceiling is small in absolute terms for fine-tuning, so a small-data explanation is AVAILABLE but remains UNTESTED AND UNASSERTED. Answering this now requires a source that fine-tunes on CTI at more than one data volume and reports calibration at each; no such source is in this base.

open_questions[6]: NEW AT CYCLE 39, RAISED BY THE ctr-0003 RESOLUTION AND NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THIS BASE. src-0001's Table 6 reports ECE and Brier Score side by side and the paper defines them identically, verbatim: 'The ECE and BS, are two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration.' BUT THE TWO METRICS ORDER THE TWO TASK FAMILIES DIFFERENTLY. On family means derived by cycle 39 from the printed cells (all AGENT-DERIVED, not printed), generation is worse than extraction on ECE at all three paradigms (0.278 vs 0.205 zero-shot, 0.320 vs 0.2425 few-shot, 0.538 vs 0.295 fine-tuned) but on Brier the gap is nil at zero-shot (0.304 vs 0.2975) and REVERSED at few-shot (0.294 vs 0.3225). A single row disagrees outright: extraction attack vector is the best-calibrated extraction cell on zero-shot ECE (0.13) and the worst on zero-shot BS (0.46). THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHICH METRIC SHOULD GOVERN A CALIBRATION CLAIM ON CTI, AND WHY. The paper does not distinguish them, offers no reliability diagram, and never comments on the divergence; this base has no source that discusses ECE-versus-Brier behaviour at all. An answer needs either a methodological source on proper scoring rules versus binned calibration error, or a CTI source reporting both metrics with a stated preference. UNTIL THEN, NO CYCLE MAY STATE AN EXTRACTION-VERSUS-GENERATION CALIBRATION GRADIENT WITHOUT NAMING THE METRIC IT HOLDS ON, and the only paradigm at which it holds on BOTH metrics is fine-tuning. This bears directly on extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis and task-dependent-reliability-framing, both of which use src-0001's extraction-versus-generation split as a calibration data point; a T3 targeting either must read this before citing it. NOTE THAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH THE CONSISTENCY HALF, where the CI widths of 0.02 against 0.06 are a single measurement with no competing metric. === CYCLE 62 NARROWS THIS SUBSTANTIALLY AND SUPPLIES THE FIRST OUTSIDE DATA POINT THE QUESTION EVER HAD, THOUGH IT DOES NOT CLOSE IT. This question said flatly that this base 'has no source that discusses ECE-versus-Brier behaviour at all'. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE. src-0013's Table I prints ECE and Brier SIDE BY SIDE, per model, per temperature, under FOUR elicitation methods, and cycle 62 pulled two of those blocks. WHAT THE COMPARISON SHOWS: IN src-0013 THE TWO METRICS DO NOT DIVERGE. Within the Verbalized block the model ordering is identical on both -- by ECE, Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.25-0.26 < Qwen3-Coder-Next 0.41-0.42 < GPT-4o-mini 0.46-0.48; by Brier, Gemini 0.26 < Qwen 0.36-0.38 < GPT-4o-mini 0.37-0.39 -- and within the Token Probability block both metrics agree that calibration is uniformly bad (ECE 0.79-0.81, Brier 0.74-0.80) and agree on the direction of the small GPT-versus-Gemini difference. SO THE ECE/BRIER DIVERGENCE THIS QUESTION WAS BUILT ON IS NOT A GENERAL PROPERTY OF THE TWO METRICS. It is specific to src-0001's Table 6, and a successor should note WHAT IS STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT THERE: src-0001's divergence appears in AGENT-DERIVED FAMILY MEANS over four and five rows respectively, not in printed per-model values, and a mean over four heterogeneous sub-tasks is a fragile construct that one outlier row can flip -- extraction attack vector, ECE 0.13 and BS 0.46 at zero-shot, is exactly such a row and is the single largest contributor to the reversal.
